question: Teacher got a CPL 6 years ago and has never renewed. Do they have to start fresh or is there a grace period?

answer.summary: The passages do not provide a grace period for a CPL that was not renewed. Under LICN-030 §2(b)(iv), a teacher whose license expires this way may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving DPI's notice of expiration, and LICN-033 §3 allows the employing PSU to request validation of an expired CPL only if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. Whether this teacher can get back to a CPL depends on facts not yet given.

claims.text: A CPL is a five-year, renewable license, and a renewal cycle is the five-year period between renewals of a CPL.
Every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted to another type of license under SBE policy.

Teachers holding a CPL must renew it every five years. Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle (four in the license area and four general), and teachers in Pre-K through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs (three in license area, three literacy, two general). The teacher's grade band therefore determines the CEU breakdown, though the total is eight either way.

A teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least proficient on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL, defined as Proficient or higher on three of the five Professional Teaching Standards including Standard 4.

If a teacher is in the final year of a renewal cycle and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan so the teacher can renew. This option applies only in the final year of a renewal cycle, so it is unlikely to apply to a CPL that is already six years old and unrenewed, but the analyst should confirm the cycle dates.

If a teacher meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle, and the teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.
An IPL is a three-year, nonrenewable license.

The governing body of a PSU may request that DPI validate an expired CPL, even without the requisite CEUs, provided the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the relevant renewal requirements by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.

The passages do not provide any grace period for renewal of an expired CPL, and they do not state that the educator must restart all licensure requirements from the beginning. The closest provisions are the IPL eligibility in LICN-030 §2(b)(iv) and validation in LICN-033 §3.
The reversion of a teacher's license from CPL to IPL is not a demotion and does not reduce salary.

question: Teacher on an IPL has 3 years of experience at 0.5 FTE and 2 years at 1.0 FTE. How do those years count?

answer.summary: For salary experience credit under LICN-006, the 1.0 FTE years count as one year each if each had at least six calendar months of employment in a fiscal year (July 1 to June 30). The 0.5 FTE years count as one year each only if they were about 12 months of employment, because 12 months at 50% equals six full-time-equivalent months; shorter periods combine with other partial years. The passages do not show how the three years count toward the CPL's three-year licensed teaching requirement, and the answer needs each year's dates and weekly hours.

claims.text: Under LICN-006 §I(a), full-time work of at least six calendar months within one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30) earns one year of experience credit, excluding one-teacher private school experience.

Under LICN-006 §I(a), a calendar month is the number of days employed divided by the number of days in the pay period, multiplied by the employee's percentage of employment. So a 0.5 FTE employee working 12 months accrues 12 × 0.5 = 6 full-time-equivalent months, which meets the six-month threshold for one year; 9 months at 0.5 accrues 4.5 months and does not.

Under LICN-006 §I(b), part-time work requires a minimum of 15 hours per week to establish experience credit in a school unit, and one year can be earned if part-time experience totals six calendar months of full-time experience within a single fiscal year. The passages do not convert 0.5 FTE into weekly hours, so the analyst must confirm the hours.

Under LICN-006 §I(c), partial years of full-time or part-time experience can be combined. Two years of part-time work can make one year if equivalent to six months of full-time experience, and partial full-time experience under six months can combine with another partial year to equal one year.

Applying these rules to the stated facts: each 1.0 FTE year yields 12 full-time-equivalent months if employed the full fiscal year, which equals two years of credit overall if both are full-time years of at least six months. Each 0.5 FTE year yields one year only if it is about 12 months of employment and meets the 15-hour minimum. Otherwise the partial periods are combined under §I(c). The maximum on these facts is 3 + 2 = 5 years, which is an upper bound and not a confirmed count.

Experience credit is not awarded for leave of absence periods, except as required by Workmen's Compensation and USERRA. Tutor, clerical paraprofessional, and substitute service is not recognized as professional educator experience.

The CPL requires at least three years of licensed teaching experience, along with completing other conditions. The passages do not define how part-time or partial-year service counts toward that three-year requirement.
An IPL is a three-year, nonrenewable license, and the passages do not say that IPL service time is counted differently for experience credit.

claims.text: LICN-033 §3 allows a PSU governing body to request DPI validation of an expired CPL issued under its employment, even if the educator does not have the requisite CEUs, provided the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year.

A school psychologist license requires preparation at the advanced/specialist or doctoral degree level, which places the school psychologist license within the student services personnel license policy.

Each person holding a student services personnel license must renew that license every five years, and student services personnel must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four aligned with the NC standards for the relevant professional discipline (EVAL policy) and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.

Under the CEU definition, one CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education or ten clock hours of professional development programming. The 18 CEUs reported therefore exceed the eight CEUs required for one LICN-032 renewal cycle by 10 CEUs, but the passages do not say whether that excess or the CEUs earned during the lapse carry forward.
LICN-033 §3 expressly permits validation without the requisite CEUs, so the CEUs earned during the lapse are not a prerequisite for validation under that section.

A teacher who meets the criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan has the license expire at the end of the renewal cycle, and may apply for an IPL 30 days after notice of expiration. This applies to teachers under LICN-030, not student services personnel.
Every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire unless renewed, extended, or converted under SBE policy.

question: A teacher with a BS in English is teaching Spanish I on a lateral basis for the rest of the year. Is that allowed and for how long?

claims.text: The passages do not contain a license type called a "lateral" license. Lateral entry licenses under G.S. 115C-297 were repealed by S.L. 2017-189, and the current policies mention them only for people who held one before that repeal.

A permit to teach may be requested by the employing public school unit for an applicant who holds at least a bachelor's degree and has never been issued any other North Carolina professional educator license. The permit is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested and cannot be extended or renewed.

An emergency license may be requested for an applicant who holds a bachelor's degree with at least 18 credit hours of coursework relevant to the licensure area, has not completed a recognized educator preparation program in that area, and does not qualify for a residency license. It is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be extended or renewed.
A person who holds or previously held a residency license cannot receive a permit to teach or an emergency license in the same license area.

Spanish is a listed secondary teaching area, and Spanish is also a special subject area. For secondary Spanish, the required test is Praxis 5195 with a score of 168, or the ACTFL OPI & WPT at Advanced Low.

question: Holds a Permit to Teach, has a bachelor's, wants to teach two more years. Can the permit be renewed?

answer.summary: A Permit to Teach cannot be extended or renewed. It is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year it was requested for, so it cannot cover two more years of teaching. Any longer-term plan would need a different license, and the passages do not say whether a new permit can be requested for a later year.

A residency license may be requested for an applicant who meets G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5) and has either completed at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area or passed the applicable licensure examination requirements. The request must come from the employing public school unit.

An emergency license may be requested for an applicant who holds a bachelor's degree with at least 18 relevant credit hours, has not completed a recognized educator preparation program in that area, and does not qualify for a residency license. It is also valid only until June 30 of the requested fiscal year and cannot be extended or renewed.

answer.summary: Under current policy, National Board certification can satisfy all eight CEUs, but only for the renewal cycle in which the certification was received, or for two CEUs in the cycle in which it is renewed. Whether the 2019 certification helps the upcoming renewal depends on which renewal cycle 2019 falls in and whether the certification has been renewed since.

If the teacher is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan and does not meet the renewal criteria, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle.

question: CPL renewal due in June. Has 7 CEUs. Good to renew?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

answer.summary: As stated, the teacher does not meet the teacher CEU requirement: 7 CEUs is one short of the 8 required, whatever the grade band. Renewal could still proceed if an exemption applies, if the teacher earns at least one more CEU in the cycle, or if the teacher meets the evaluation requirement and is handled under the mandatory improvement plan rules.

claims.text: A teacher holding a CPL must renew it every five years and must complete eight CEUs during each renewal cycle.

Pre-K through Grade 5 teachers need 3 CEUs in their license area, 3 literacy CEUs, and 2 general CEUs (3+3+2=8). Grades 6 through 12 teachers need 4 license-area CEUs and 4 general CEUs (4+4=8). Either way the total is 8, so 7 CEUs is 1 short.

One CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education or ten clock hours of professional development. The teacher's 7 CEUs equal 70 clock hours, and one more CEU (10 clock hours, or two-thirds of a semester credit hour) would meet the total of 8.
A license expires June 30 of the year it is set to expire unless it is renewed or converted under SBE policy. A June renewal is therefore timely only if the requirements are met by then.

Teachers employed by a local board must have a rating of at least "proficient" on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL. That means "Proficient" or higher on at least three of the five Professional Teaching Standards, including Standard 4.

If a local-board teacher in the final year of a renewal cycle was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan so the teacher can renew. The teacher then receives an IPL, not a CPL, and may apply for a CPL at the end of the IPL term if the requirements, including the required CEUs, are met.

If a teacher meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle. The teacher can apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving the expiration notice. The 7-CEU teacher does not meet Section 1, so this provision is not directly triggered by the CEU count alone.
A General Assembly member is exempt from the teacher CEU requirement for a renewal cycle in which the member serves, if the member notifies DPI during that cycle.
A teacher who holds or renews National Board certification gets credit for all 8 CEUs in the cycle of initial certification, or 2 CEUs in the cycle of renewal.
Mandatory training hours count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by the local board as a condition of employment, and the educator otherwise meets the renewal requirements.
A CEU may be earned through college or university credit or professional development programs.

question: School counselor candidate, master's in school counseling, 2 years experience. What NC license do they need?

answer.summary: A school counselor candidate with a master's in school counseling would apply for a student services personnel license (school counselor classification). Whether it is an initial professional license (IPL) or a continuing professional license (CPL) depends on whether they have already passed the school counselor exam (Praxis 5422, score 159).

To qualify for a student services personnel license, an applicant must have completed an educator preparation program at the master's (M-Level), specialist, or doctoral level. A master's degree in school counseling meets the degree level requirement, provided the program is an EPP.
The license is issued at the highest degree level at which the applicant completed an EPP, so a master's-level EPP completion supports an M-level license.
An EPP that the license requires must be recognized by the SBE or by the equivalent licensing authority of the jurisdiction where the EPP has its principal place of business.
The School Counselor licensure test is Praxis 5422 (licensure code 005), with a required score of 159.

Exam timing: the applicant must satisfy the exam requirements before or during the third year of licensure and must attempt the exam at least once during the first year. If the exam is already satisfied before applying, DPI issues a CPL. If not satisfied but otherwise qualified, DPI issues an IPL.

A continuing professional administrator or student services personnel license requires satisfying the applicable exam requirements on the same timing rules and meeting the other requirements in LICN-012.

The policies provided do not set a years-of-experience requirement for a student services personnel license. The three-year teaching experience and Beginning Teacher Support Program requirements in LICN-024 §1 apply to teacher licenses, not to student services personnel licenses.

Two years of experience matters for salary credit, not for license type. Full-time work of at least six calendar months within a fiscal year earns one year of experience credit, so two qualifying full-time fiscal years would earn two years of credit.

question: Teacher's CPL lapsed three years ago. Taught four years before that. What's the reinstatement process?

answer.summary: The passages do not give a general reinstatement process for a lapsed CPL. The possible routes depend on why the license lapsed and on the educator's employment since then: a PSU-requested validation under LICN-033 §3 (only if not employed by any PSU in the preceding fiscal year), eligibility to apply for an IPL under LICN-030 §2(b)(iv) (which is tied to a renewal cycle and LSAU action), or a discipline-based petition under LICN-007 §8 (only for a revoked license or denied application). Confirm the reason for the lapse and the employment history before choosing a route.

claims.text: LICN-033 §3 allows the governing body of a PSU to request that DPI validate an expired CPL issued under its employment, even if the educator lacks the required CEUs, provided the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year.

A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the renewal requirements in LICN-030, LICN-031, or LICN-032 by the end of the third year to renew the CPL for a new five-year renewal cycle.

Applied to this teacher, the validation route depends on whether the teacher was employed by any PSU in the fiscal year before the request. The analyst's facts (lapse three years ago, teaching four years before that) do not say whether the teacher has worked for a PSU since the lapse. Also, a PSU must make the request, so the teacher cannot apply directly under this section.

A teacher who meets the renewal criteria in Section 1 but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU has the license expire at the end of the renewal cycle. That teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.
A teacher whose license reverted from CPL to IPL is not demoted in rank and does not lose salary, but this provision concerns reversion and does not describe reinstatement of a lapsed CPL.

The reinstatement petition in LICN-007 §8 applies only to a license that has been revoked or to an application that has been denied under LICN-007. The teacher may petition no sooner than 12 months after the effective date of the revocation or denial.

A reinstatement petition must be submitted in writing to the Superintendent with a statement explaining why the circumstances that led to revocation or denial no longer justify prohibiting the petitioner from holding a license. The Superintendent may deny, grant, or grant on probation, and a probationary grant is reviewed one year later.

A CPL is renewed every five years. Renewal requires 8 CEUs per cycle. For Grades 6-12 teachers, that is 4 CEUs in the license area plus 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment (4 + 4 = 8). Grades PK-5 teachers need 3 literacy, 3 license-area, and 2 general CEUs (3 + 3 + 2 = 8).

A teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least "proficient" on the most recent annual evaluation in NCEES to renew a CPL. Proficient means a rating of Proficient or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Standard 4.
A CPL renewal under LICN-030 also requires the teacher to have completed a continuing professional development plan aligned with the Professional Teaching Standards, as stated in LICN-030 §2(a).
The policies provided do not define the term "lapse" or distinguish it from "expiration." They also do not describe a general reinstatement process for a CPL that lapsed through non-renewal.

question: Applicant from Georgia, 2 years of teaching, needs NC license. What do they qualify for?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

answer.summary: A Georgia applicant with 2 years of experience would most likely qualify for an Initial Professional License (IPL), not a Continuing Professional License (CPL), if the 2 years is licensed professional experience and they either hold a Georgia license in the corresponding area or completed a recognized educator preparation program. Eligibility and the exam path depend on facts not yet provided, including license status, license area, degree level, and exam results.

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant is one who completed an educator or administrator preparation program with a principal place of business outside North Carolina. Whether this applicant is out-of-state depends on where their preparation program is based.

An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an initial professional license (IPL). Two years is less than three, so the IPL track applies if the 2 years is licensed professional educator experience. Experience that was not licensed does not count toward this threshold under the cited text.

To qualify for an IPL, the applicant must either hold a license in the corresponding license area in a jurisdiction outside North Carolina (for example, a Georgia license), or have completed an educator preparation program recognized by the jurisdiction where that program has its principal place of business.

An applicant with a clear license from another jurisdiction and fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience there may also qualify for an IPL. An applicant who completed an EPP based outside North Carolina may also qualify.
A CPL requires more than three years of licensed professional educator experience for out-of-state applicants. At 2 years, this applicant does not yet qualify for a CPL under the out-of-state rule.

Exam requirements for an out-of-state IPL: an applicant qualifying for an IPL in Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum must meet the applicable North Carolina exam requirements by the end of the third year of licensure, regardless of any out-of-state exam passed. For any other license area, the applicant must either pass an out-of-state exam for that area in the examining jurisdiction, or meet the NC exam requirements before or during the third year, provided the NC exams were attempted at least once during the first year.
Out-of-state exam results must be presented at the time of initial NC licensure. An out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

Under the general IPL conversion rule, the IPL may be converted to a clear CPL if the required State Board exam is taken at least once during the first year and passed before or during the third year.

A teacher license is available only at the highest degree level at which the applicant completed an EPP (Bachelor's, Master's, Specialist, or Doctoral). The applicant's degree level therefore determines the level of license and affects salary placement.
The fee for an Out-of-State Initial Professional License application opened by an individual educator is $70 for in-state and $100 for out-of-state, based on the fee table effective January 1, 2017.

If the applicant is an active-duty servicemember or spouse, the NC policy allows out-of-state exam scores from a different jurisdiction than the EPP location, and the out-of-state license may be recognized until the military orders expire or June 30 of the fiscal year in which they expire, whichever is later.

question: Teacher has an Initial Professional License in elementary ed and wants the EC general curriculum add-on. Doable?

answer.summary: The add-on is possible only by passing the licensure exams, not by completing coursework, because Exceptional Children: General Curriculum is excluded from the coursework route. The teacher must also have already met the exam requirements for the elementary area on the IPL. Confirm both exam statuses before advising.

claims.text: An applicant may add a new license area to an IPL only if the applicant has met the licensure examination requirements for the initial license area.

For Exceptional Children: General Curriculum, an applicant may add the area only by satisfying the applicable licensure examination requirements and cannot add it through coursework alone.

Because the initial area is Elementary Education, the teacher must have met the elementary exam requirements before the add-on can be made to the IPL. Elementary (K-6) requires Pearson Test 890 Foundations of Reading with a score of 233, and either Pearson Test 203 Mathematics or Praxis 7813 CKT Math with a score of 227 or 150 respectively.

The EC General Curriculum exam requirements listed for code 88091 include Foundational Knowledge Test 5355 with a score of 145, Pearson Test 890 Foundations of Reading with a score of 233, and Pearson Test 203 Mathematics or Praxis 7813 CKT Math with a score of 227 or 150.
The Exceptional Children: General Curriculum license area is a valid teacher license area under the Exceptional Children (Kindergarten through Grade 12) classification.

question: PTT expired 2 months ago. Can they reinstate?

answer.summary: The passages do not define "PTT" and do not describe reinstating a license that has simply expired. question: Preschool teacher with BS in child development wants to lateral-enter Birth-K. Eligible?

answer.summary: The passages do not support a 'lateral entry' route; that license was repealed by S.L. 2017-189. She could qualify for a standard Birth-K teacher license if her BS came from a recognized educator preparation program covering Birth-K, and no licensure test is required for that area. Otherwise, the options are a residency, emergency, or permit to teach, each with conditions, so confirm her program, prior NC licensure, and coursework before advising.

claims.text: The Birth through Kindergarten teacher license is a current classification (license code 14) that requires no licensure test and no required score.

A teacher license requires completion of an educator preparation program at the bachelor's (A-Level) or higher level, except as provided in Section 5 of the policy. A BS qualifies only if it was completed through a recognized EPP.
An applicant is eligible only for a license at the highest degree level at which she completed an EPP, so a BS-level EPP completion supports an A-level Birth-K license.
Any person employed as a professional educator in a NC public school must hold, or be qualified to hold, a DPI professional educator license.
The lateral entry license under G.S. 115C-297 was repealed by S.L. 2017-189. The passages describe lateral entry only as a status for people who held that license earlier, not as a current pathway.

Standard Birth-K licensure via an EPP is possible only if her BS program was a recognized EPP completed in or covering the Birth-K area. The passages do not say what Birth-K coursework is required within a BS program.

If she has not completed a recognized Birth-K EPP, a residency license may be requested by a PSU if she has completed at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area or passed the applicable licensure exam. The residency license also depends on G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5), which is not in the passages.
An emergency license requires a bachelor's degree with at least 18 relevant credit hours, no completed recognized EPP in that licensure area, and no eligibility for a residency license.

A permit to teach requires a bachelor's degree and that she has never been issued any other NC professional educator license. It is valid only until June 30 of the requested fiscal year and cannot be renewed.
A person who holds or previously held a residency license is not eligible for a permit to teach or emergency license in the same license area.

A limited license applies only to teaching areas and to certain former lateral-entry holders who are currently employed by the PSU. It is not an available route unless she previously held that lateral entry license.
Residency license holders must receive 10 days of professional development and at least 3 hours of field experience before classroom teaching, plus 10 hours of field experience during the first year.

question: Teacher has a CPL in science and wants to add math 6-9. How many credits?

answer.summary: The teacher can add middle grades (6-9) Mathematics to a CPL in one of two ways: complete 24 credit hours of higher-education coursework in the license area with a grade of C or better in each course, or pass the required exam (Praxis 5164, score 157). Middle grades Mathematics (Grade 6 to Grade 9) is a recognized teaching license area.

question: Teacher on a limited license for a special subject, 3 years in. Can they keep renewing it?

answer.summary: A limited license is a three-year renewable license, and renewal requires the employing unit to file an affidavit that the teacher is currently employed, is effective, and will be encouraged to pursue a CPL, plus EVAAS growth where data exists. Whether this teacher can keep renewing depends on their current employment, effectiveness, EVAAS data, and whether they have passed the licensure exam, none of which the analyst has provided.

claims.text: A limited license is defined as a three-year renewable license issued to an individual who has completed an EPP but has not satisfied the applicable licensure examination requirements.

A limited license may only be issued for teaching license areas, not for administrator or student services personnel license areas. Special Subjects (Kindergarten – Grade 12) is a teaching classification, so a special subject area can qualify.

To renew a limited license, the employing PSU governing body must submit an affidavit to DPI, signed by the licensee's supervising principal and the local superintendent, attesting that the licensee is currently employed by the PSU, is an effective teacher, and that the PSU will encourage the licensee to pursue a CPL.

To renew a limited license, the licensee must meet or exceed expected growth as measured by EVAAS, where such data is available. If there is more than one year of growth data, DPI averages it. Data is limited to the years since the limited license was first issued or its most recent prior renewal, and DPI does not consider EVAAS data from 2019-2020 or 2020-2021.
The passages do not say what happens to a special subject teacher who has no EVAAS data, since the EVAAS requirement applies only where such data is available.

A teacher on a limited license originally qualified under the lateral entry pathway (a former G.S. 115C-297 lateral entry license), while the initial limited license criteria are in LICN-023 §1(b), which requires current employment with the PSU and an affidavit from the superintendent and principal. The §1(a) criteria cite G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a), which the passages do not set out.

The passages do not say what occurs when a limited license holder passes the required examination, although the definition ties limited license status to not having satisfied the examination requirements.

A teacher with a limited license is not one of the IPL/CPL holders covered by the CPL conversion or renewal rules in LICN-024 or LICN-030, so those CPL requirements do not apply directly to limited license renewal.

question: International applicant, bachelor's from India, 6 years teaching math there, wants NC license. Next steps?

answer.summary: Whether this applicant can get a North Carolina license, and which kind, depends on facts not yet provided: whether the 6 years of teaching were under a valid Indian teaching license, whether the bachelor's came from a teacher preparation program, and whether they hold a passing math exam score. claims.text: For licensing purposes, an out-of-state applicant includes any applicant who completed an educator or administrator preparation program with a principal place of business outside North Carolina, and this expressly includes international preparation programs.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a continuing professional license (CPL) if they meet both LICN-025 §2 criteria. The three-year threshold counts licensed experience, so unlicensed teaching does not count toward it.

The first CPL criterion requires a clear license from a jurisdiction other than North Carolina. A clear license must be in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, free of any pending unprofessional-conduct investigation in any state, and not voluntarily surrendered during such an investigation.

The second CPL criterion is met either by holding National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification, or by showing the other jurisdiction's requirements are substantially similar. Substantially similar means the applicant had to complete an EPP recognized by the state where it is located, and pass an out-of-state exam for each license area sought.

If the applicant has fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience, the out-of-state route is an initial professional license (IPL). That route requires either a license in the corresponding area from the other jurisdiction, or completion of an EPP recognized by the jurisdiction where it is located. Under LICN-020 §1(b), an EPP based outside North Carolina also qualifies an applicant for an IPL.
Out-of-state exam results must be presented at the time of initial licensure in North Carolina. Those results cannot be used to convert an IPL to a CPL.

A teacher license requires completion of an educator preparation program at the level sought. A bachelor's degree qualifies only at the A level, and an applicant is eligible only at the highest degree level at which they completed an EPP. A bachelor's degree alone, without a completed EPP, does not meet this requirement.

The out-of-state initial professional license application fee is $100 on the fee schedule. That schedule reflects applications opened effective January 1, 2017, and the passages do not list a CPL fee.

Under LICN-026, an international faculty license is available only to a foreign national holding a J-1 visa who does not meet the requirements for any other DPI license. That option is relevant only if the applicant holds a J-1 visa and no other license route applies.
The testing table in LICN-003 lists required tests and scores by license area, but the passages provided do not show the secondary math row, so the required math exam cannot be confirmed from them.

Under an emergency license, the salary level is A-level, but the applicant may still qualify for experience pay under LICN-006.
Under an international faculty license, the salary level is A-level with zero years, but years taught in a PSU on that license can accumulate toward State Salary Schedule experience.

Without a master's degree, graduate degree salary pay is not available; it requires a master's or higher degree that meets the LICN-006 criteria. A teacher license is issued only at the highest degree level completed, so a bachelor's-level applicant is eligible only at the bachelor's level.
